newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Sen. Murkowski to make statement on Pena.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Sen. Murkowski to make statement on Pena.

text.p: U.S. Senate Energy Committee Chairman Frank Murkowski, who has stalled Federico Pena's nomination to be Secretary of Energy, said he will make a statement and answer reporters' questions on the issue on Tuesday.

Murkowski in a statement said he will hold a news conference to discuss two topics, namely the nomination of Federico Pena to be Secretary of Energy and the necessity for safer storage of high-level radioactive waste.
Murkowski, an Alaska Republican, has twice cancelled meetings for votes his committee must make to move Pena's nomination on to the full Senate for confirmation.
He has not yet rescheduled another vote.
In a letter to committee Democrats who were irritated by the delay, Murkowski said he wanted to know whether he would be able to work with Pena on the nuclear waste issue.
He also insisted that the Clinton administration must offer a plan to manage the waste accumulating at nuclear power plants which the federal government is supposed to take control of next year.

Murkowski has been angry that President Clinton threatened to veto his bill to establish a temporary dump for nuclear waste in Nevada while the government pursues a long-term storage project that is not expected to be ready to accept the waste until 2010.
The White House said Murkowski's bill would divert resources from the long-term project.
